analysis.title: Market Update November 2026: S&P 500 Equal- vs. Market-Capitalization-Weighted
key_insights: The global economy has stayed robust, with positive leading indicators and high investment levels supporting U.S. growth in particular.
The current earnings season has been encouraging: many companies exceeded expectations and earnings growth has spread across more sectors.
Market breadth has visibly increased recently.
Headwinds came from persistently elevated interest rates and rising energy prices. Middle East geopolitical tensions added uncertainty at times.
Core inflation continued to moderate in many industrialized countries, and long-term inflation expectations have stayed stable despite higher energy prices.
Reichmuth remains constructive on equities for the coming months. Broad earnings growth supports the view, while high interest rates and geopolitical risks are likely to cause volatility.
The U.S. midterm elections could add momentum. Historically, stocks have performed well in the twelve months after midterms, and political uncertainty has tended to subside.
Market direction will depend on how geopolitical tensions around the war in Iran evolve after the midterms.

The AI cycle is likely to continue. After large investments in semiconductors, data centers and power infrastructure, attention is shifting to which companies can use AI productively. Reichmuth sees opportunities in banking and biotechnology.
Since early October, the equally weighted S&P 500 has outperformed the market-cap-weighted index, which indicates companies outside the largest tech stocks are contributing more to the rally.
Broader participation reduces dependence on a few heavyweights. The open question is whether broader earnings growth can be sustained in coming quarters.

Portfolio view: overweight equities with themes in high-dividend quality Swiss stocks, energy and healthcare as diversifiers, emerging market shares focused on Asia, and companies benefiting from the investment boom.
Portfolio view: avoid long-duration government bonds in EUR and USD because high government spending is leading investors to demand higher risk premiums.

Portfolio view: gold is consolidating at high levels and Reichmuth expects the bull market to continue after this phase. Metals benefit from electrification, infrastructure and digitalization demand and face a supply deficit.
Portfolio view: global real estate no longer benefits from structural appreciation, with Switzerland the exception. In alternatives, hedge funds and infrastructure are preferred over private credit.
